quests.instruction: Find the month the branch will realistically open.
quests.hint: Each new piece of information moves the date later. Follow the chain to the last estimate.
quests.explanation: June is correct. March and April were earlier expectations that were replaced as the delays were explained.
quests.textToSpeak: The board initially proposed opening the new branch in March. Then the landlord delayed the lease, so April looked likely. But the contractors said the fit-out would take at least ten weeks, and after that the license inspection could add another fortnight. So realistically, it'll be June before the doors open.

quests.instruction: Notice who has already signed the budget.
quests.hint: Several people are involved, but only one has completed an action. Separate what is done from what is still pending.
quests.explanation: The client's legal team has not reviewed the budget yet. So the answer is the finance director.
quests.textToSpeak: I asked Dana whether the client had approved the budget, and she said not yet. Then Marcus said the finance director had signed it last night, but it still has to go through the client's legal team, which usually takes about a week.

quests.instruction: Find which recommendation was postponed.
quests.hint: Three items are listed, and two are accepted by number. Work out which one is left.
quests.explanation: The first and third recommendations were accepted, so the second was delayed. So the answer is the app.
quests.textToSpeak: The consultant recommended three changes: shorten the onboarding from two weeks to one, replace the paper forms with an app, and reduce the number of approval levels. Management accepted the first and third, but postponed the app until next year because of the cost.

quests.instruction: Listen for what disqualifies you from the tax credit.
quests.hint: Two conditions qualify you. One condition cancels it. Listen for ‘but not if’.
quests.explanation: The answer is a claim in the past two years. Six months of work and full-time study are the ways to qualify.
quests.textToSpeak: You can claim the tax credit if you worked at least six months last year, or if you were a full-time student, but not if you had already claimed it in the past two years, regardless of your income.
quests.targetDetail: a claim in the past two years
options: a claim in the past two years

quests.instruction: Wipe the glass and tap what checking a bag costs for the round trip.
quests.hint: The fee is given per direction. Think about how many directions a round trip has.
quests.explanation: The answer is $80. Forty dollars each way, in both directions, makes eighty.
quests.textToSpeak: The airline said my baggage limit is twenty-three kilos, but the ticket I bought is the basic fare, which only allows a cabin bag of eight. To check a bag, I'd have to pay forty dollars each way.

quests.instruction: Listen for how they solved the space problem.
quests.hint: The problem is stated with two numbers. The solution comes in the final sentence.
quests.explanation: An overflow room is correct. They kept the original hall and added a second one for the extra guests.
quests.textToSpeak: Nobody argued about the date. What people questioned was the venue, since the hall holds a hundred and twenty, but around a hundred and fifty had said they'd come. In the end they agreed to rent the neighboring hall as an overflow room.

quests.instruction: Spot when they finally decided to leave.
quests.hint: The departure time changes twice. Only the last change counts.
quests.explanation: Correct: 5:30. Six and six thirty were earlier plans, replaced because of the ferry schedule.
quests.textToSpeak: So the plan was to leave at six, but Ines needed to pick up her sister, so we said half past six. Then it turned out the ferry only runs on the hour, so we're leaving at five thirty to be safe, and Ines will meet us there.

quests.instruction: Listen for the house the parcel was wrongly delivered to.
quests.hint: The speaker's own address and the wrong address use the same digits. Know which is which.
quests.explanation: Number 12 is correct. Number twenty-one is the speaker's real address.
quests.textToSpeak: I never received the parcel, so I contacted the courier, who said it was delivered to number twelve. But my address is number twenty-one, so the driver must have swapped the digits.

quests.instruction: Wipe away the fog and tap when the museum closes on Thursdays.
quests.hint: There is an old schedule, a new schedule, and a special day. The special day has its own time.
quests.explanation: The answer is 8:00. Six is the new normal closing time, while five was the old one.
quests.textToSpeak: The museum's opening hours changed in spring. It used to open at nine and close at five, but now it opens at ten, closes at six, and stays open until eight on Thursdays.

quests.instruction: Notice the notice period in the signed contract.
quests.hint: Three versions have three numbers. Only the signed one matters.
quests.explanation: 90 days is correct. Thirty and sixty were earlier drafts.
quests.textToSpeak: The first draft of the contract said thirty days' notice, the second said sixty, and the version we signed says ninety, though either side can waive it in writing.

quests.instruction: Find what they did instead of trekking.
quests.hint: One activity was replaced, and another was only kept as a possibility.
quests.explanation: The answer is a cooking course. The beach days were still uncertain.
quests.textToSpeak: We had hoped the rainy season would have ended by the time we arrived, but it hadn't, so we swapped the trekking for a cooking course, and kept the beach for the last two days in case the weather improved.

quests.instruction: Listen for the biggest complaint in the survey.
quests.hint: One item is denied, one is first, and one was wrongly expected to be first.
quests.explanation: The answer is the waiting time. The price is denied, and staff attitude ranked third.
quests.textToSpeak: According to the survey, the biggest complaint was not the price but the waiting time, followed by the quality of the food. Staff attitude, which management expected to top the list, came a distant third.

quests.instruction: Find what both terms describe.
quests.hint: Two different labels describe the same idea. The explanation comes at the end.
quests.explanation: The answer is first-time customers. Both terms refer to people who have never purchased before.
quests.textToSpeak: The two departments seem to be saying the same thing in different words. Marketing calls it customer acquisition, while sales talks about new accounts. In practice, they both mean people who've never bought from us before.

quests.instruction: Listen for the closing time the staff confirmed.
quests.hint: Three sources disagree. One person of authority settles it.
quests.explanation: The staff said the website is right and the sign is outdated. So the answer is 8:00.
quests.textToSpeak: It's a bit odd, actually. The shop says it's open till nine, the website says eight, and the sign on the door says seven. The staff said the door sign is out of date, and the website is right.

quests.instruction: Tap how many people were on the trip at the end.
quests.hint: The group shrinks and then grows. Follow every change in order.
quests.explanation: 8 is correct. Twelve minus three is nine, minus two is seven, plus one is eight.
quests.textToSpeak: There were originally twelve of us. Three dropped out before the trip, two more got sick on the first day, and a friend of a friend joined us halfway through. So by the end there were eight of us.

quests.instruction: Listen for when you should skip a missed dose.
quests.hint: The general rule has one exception. Listen for ‘unless’.
quests.explanation: Otherwise you take the missed dose immediately. So the answer is if the next dose is near.
quests.textToSpeak: The medication should be taken with food, and never with grapefruit juice, since it interferes with absorption. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, unless it's almost time for the next one.
quests.targetDetail: if the next dose is near
options: if the next dose is near

quests.instruction: Wipe away the fog and tap what members paid.
quests.hint: Each group has its own rule. Apply the correct discount to the base price.
quests.explanation: The answer is $120. A forty percent discount on two hundred is eighty, so members pay one hundred twenty.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd assumed the conference was free, but registration was two hundred, though members got a forty percent discount, and students, who normally paid half, were let in free this year.

quests.instruction: Notice the decade the story jumps back to.
quests.hint: The story moves through three periods. The flashback is the middle one.
quests.explanation: The answer is the 1930s. Nineteen forty-five is where the novel begins.
quests.textToSpeak: The novel opens in nineteen forty-five, jumps back to the author's childhood in the thirties, and finally returns to the present day, so you have to pay attention to the dates to follow it.

quests.instruction: Wipe the glass, then tap when the road work will now be done.
quests.hint: A concession leads to a change of schedule. Follow ‘which means’.
quests.explanation: The day lane stays open, so the work moves to the night. So the answer is at night.
quests.textToSpeak: After protests from local shops, the council agreed to keep one lane open during the day, which means the work will now be done at night and will take about four months longer.

quests.instruction: Listen for the flight time.
quests.hint: Three people give three different times. The last sentence names who was correct.
quests.explanation: 7:15 is correct. The speaker's own time and Omar's time were both wrong.
quests.textToSpeak: Lena thought the flight was at seven fifteen, Omar thought seven fifty, and I said it was at seventeen fifteen, which is actually a quarter past five in the afternoon. Turns out Lena was right.

quests.instruction: Identify what the speaker says matters most.
quests.hint: The obvious answer is rejected. The example that follows supports the real answer.
quests.explanation: A longer term can cost more even at a lower rate. So the answer is the length of the loan.
quests.textToSpeak: It's not the interest rate that matters most, but the length of the loan. A lower rate over thirty years can cost more in total than a slightly higher rate over twenty.

quests.instruction: Focus on what a former employee applying for the senior role must submit.
quests.hint: Start with the basic list, add the extra for the senior role, then remove what the exception allows.
quests.explanation: The answer is a résumé and a portfolio. Former employees can skip the references, but the senior role needs the portfolio.
quests.textToSpeak: Every applicant must submit a résumé and two references. Those applying for the senior role also need a portfolio, and anyone who has previously worked here can skip the references.

quests.instruction: Clear the glass and tap when the security camera shows the car leaving.
quests.hint: Two people give estimates, and a camera gives another time. Which source is the question about?
quests.explanation: Correct: 7:55. Eight and seven forty are the witnesses' statements.
quests.textToSpeak: At the hearing, the first witness said she saw the car at eight, but the second witness, who lives across the street, said it was already gone by seven forty. The security camera, however, shows it leaving at seven fifty-five.

quests.instruction: Listen for who encouraged the speaker to follow music.
quests.hint: Three relatives have three opinions. ‘Of all people’ signals a surprise.
quests.explanation: The answer is the grandmother. The parents' hopes were about other careers.
quests.textToSpeak: My mother assumed I'd be studying medicine, my father hoped for engineering, but my grandmother, of all people, was the one who encouraged me to follow music.

quests.instruction: Wipe away the fog and tap what happens right after the keynote.
quests.hint: The printed schedule is outdated. Rebuild the order using the correction.
quests.explanation: Lunch is correct. The parallel sessions were moved to later in the day.
quests.textToSpeak: According to the schedule, the keynote comes first, then two parallel sessions, then lunch. But the schedule's outdated. The parallel sessions have been moved to after lunch, so lunch now follows the keynote directly.

quests.instruction: Focus on the total the speaker will pay.
quests.hint: Follow the order of operations: discount first, tax second.
quests.explanation: The answer is $4,180. Four thousand minus five percent is 3,800. Ten percent tax adds 380.
quests.textToSpeak: It cost less than I feared. The quote was four thousand, plus ten percent tax, but they've offered a five percent discount for paying upfront, and that's calculated before tax. So I'm paying just under four thousand two hundred.

quests.instruction: Identify where the locals eat.
quests.hint: A tourist assumption is rejected. Listen for where the locals go.
quests.explanation: The old town is what tourists assume. So the answer is the harbor district.
quests.textToSpeak: Contrary to what most tourists assume, the old town isn't the best place to eat. The locals go to the harbor district, where the prices are lower and the portions are larger, though you'll need a reservation on weekends.

quests.instruction: Catch the start date of the workshop.
quests.hint: A correction is given with ‘not’. Track the confirmed date, not the rejected one.
quests.explanation: Correct: the 12th. The tenth was the earlier date. Two is the number of days.
quests.textToSpeak: Just to confirm the final arrangement: the workshop will run for two days rather than three, beginning on the twelfth, not the tenth. Lunch is included on the first day only, and the certificate will be emailed within a week of completion.

quests.instruction: Wipe the glass and tap why the finance team's summary was misleading.
quests.hint: The first summary is contradicted. The reason is introduced by ‘only because’.
quests.explanation: It left out the lease is correct. That cost made the profit picture look better than it was.
quests.textToSpeak: I had a look at the numbers again. Revenue was up eight percent, but costs were up eleven, so margins actually shrank. The finance team's initial summary said profits improved, but that was only because they left out the new warehouse lease.

quests.instruction: Identify the date the conference will finally take place.
quests.hint: Three dates appear as the plan changes twice. The last change is final.
quests.explanation: The fourth and the eleventh are the earlier dates, before the venue flooded. So the answer is the 25th.
quests.textToSpeak: We were advised to book flights early, but then the dates of the conference changed twice. First it moved from the fourth to the eleventh, then, after the venue flooded, to the twenty-fifth. So, thankfully, my refundable ticket is now for the twenty-fifth.
